c74object.name: evi.crossover.sum~
c74object.digest: Summing, including allpass alignment, for use with evi.crossover.3band~
c74object.description:
evi.crossover.sum~ is a 'max define' for the evi_crossover_sum.gendsp gen~ abstraction. Because evi.crossover.sum~ is a 'max define' it also accepts all messages and attributes that a gen~ object does.
Linkwitz-Riley crossovers sum perfectly flat on recombination of the outputs (providing allpass alignment is used). Use evi.crossover.sum~ to sum multiband processing created with the evi.crossover.3band~ object. @see the 'seealso' section for other evieve objects that are related.

inlet.digest: Inlet #4: High Crossover Frequency in Hz @min 10 @max 20000
inlet.description: Allpass alignment requires feeding in the 'High Crossover Frequency' from the [evi.crossover.3band~] object in order to produce the correct signal.

outlet.description: Perfectly flat summed crossover bands into one signal.

attribute.name: align
attribute.description: Allpass alignment in this splitting stage off or on. This must be opposite to the equivalent attribute in the feeding [evi.crossover.3band~] object. @see 'Discussion' in the reference file for more information.

attribute.name: order
attribute.description: 0=2-pole (shallower) crossover filters, 1=4-pole (steeper) crossover filters. 2-pole can be subtle, 4-pole gives more rejection. This must be matched with the equivalent attribute in the feeding [evi.crossover.3band~] object.

c74object.discussion: As opposed to 2-band crossovers, 3-band crossovers require additional allpass alignment in order to provide flat summing. The purists will say this must be done at the recombination stage (in evi.crossover.sum~ which is designed to sum the end of processing chain from a evi.crossover.3band~ object). However, it does not matter that much, so evi.crossover.3band~ and evi.crossover.sum~ include an align attribute which lets you do allpass alignment in the split stage or the recombination stage. It is on in .3band~ and off in .sum~ by default. The align attribute should always be opposite in each object regardless of which method is used.
